caption: Lemma 2 on 1,000 ImageNet training images (1 per class of role bank (1000 classes), default_rng(0); luminance, mean removed, Hann window, 224 x 224 pixels). (a) Mean magnitude spectrum of the images, log scale, zero frequency at the centre. (b) Ratio of the mean magnitude spectra of the left-right and the up-down mirror images, log scale: it is 0 at every frequency (largest |log10 ratio| 4.3e-16), and so is the difference for every single image (largest 6.2e-16 of the image's peak magnitude). (c) The same ratio for the image rotated by 90 degrees against the original, on the same colour scale (from -0.1 to 0.1 decades): rotation swaps the two frequency axes, and the mean magnitude along the vertical frequency axis is 1.12 times that along the other (0.05 to 0.45 cycles per pixel), so the rotated spectrum differs. (d) Per image, the largest difference between the two magnitude spectra relative to the image's peak magnitude: rounding error for the two mirrors (at most 6.2e-16), a real difference for the rotation (median 0.61).
